blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A scheduler has `record Room(String name, int seats)` and `record Slot(LocalTime start, Room room)`. A slot whose room is not assigned yet holds `room == null`. The code runs `if (s instanceof Slot(var start, Room(var name, var seats))) book(start, name); else reject(s);`. What happens to `new Slot(LocalTime.of(9, 0), null)`?

options.text: It goes to `book(...)` with `name` bound to `null`, since the inner pattern first takes the room apart into `null` parts
options.says: a nested record pattern starts with an instanceof test, and null is an instance of nothing, so it never binds anything from a null component

options.text: It goes to `reject(s)`, since the inner pattern first asks whether the `null` room is a `Room`, and it is not
options.says: a record pattern never matches null at any depth; the whole pattern fails and the else branch runs

options.text: It reaches neither branch and throws `NullPointerException`, since the inner pattern first calls `name()` on the `null` room
options.says: the type test on the component fails first, so no accessor is called on a null room; the pattern just doesn't match

options.text: It reaches neither branch and throws `MatchException`, since the inner pattern first fails to take the `null` room apart
options.says: MatchException comes from an accessor that throws; a null component makes a nested pattern not match, quietly

origin.section: A Record Pattern Never Matches null, at Any Depth; var and the Component's Declared Type Do

questions.stem: A metrics exporter holds `record Sample(String name, Number value)` and runs `if (o instanceof Sample(var name, Long count)) emitCounter(name, count); else if (o instanceof Sample(var name, Double gauge)) emitGauge(name, gauge); else log.debug("skipped {}", o);`. After a library upgrade, counters arrive with an `Integer` value. What does the exporter do with them?

options.text: It emits them as counters, since `Long count` converts the `Integer` value to `Long` the way `int` widens to `long`
options.says: a type pattern on a reference component converts nothing; it asks whether the value is a Long

options.text: It reaches the last branch for each one, since `Long count` and `Double gauge` each test the value and an `Integer` fails both
options.says: a narrower type on a component is a test; an Integer fails both, and the leftover branch takes it without an error

options.text: It throws `ClassCastException` at the first test, since `Long count` casts the `Integer` value to `Long` and the cast fails
options.says: a narrower component type is a test, not a cast: a value of another class makes the pattern fail without an exception

options.text: It stops compiling after the upgrade, since `Long count` and `Double gauge` each no longer fit the value the library sends
options.says: the component is declared Number, and Long still narrows it; the compiler looks at declared types, which didn't change

origin.section: A Narrower Type on a Component Is a Test, So a Payload Whose Type Changes Stops Matching

questions.stem: `record Quote(String symbol, BigDecimal price)` overrides `price()` to throw `IllegalStateException` for a quote older than five seconds. A pricing loop runs, for each object `o`: `try { String s = switch (o) { case Quote(var symbol, var price) -> symbol + " " + price; default -> "no quote"; }; publish(s); } catch (IllegalStateException e) { skip(o); }`. A stale quote arrives. What happens?

options.text: The `default` branch publishes "no quote", since the switch treats the accessor's exception as a non-match
options.says: an accessor that throws makes the match end abruptly; no other branch is tried

options.text: The handler skips the quote, since the accessor's exception leaves the switch exactly as it was thrown
options.says: an exception from an accessor during a match arrives wrapped in MatchException, which this catch doesn't name

options.text: The loop ends with a `MatchException`, since the switch wraps the accessor's exception in that type
options.says: the match ends with MatchException, the IllegalStateException as its cause; the catch for IllegalStateException doesn't run

options.text: The case publishes the symbol with `null`, since the switch binds `price` without calling `price()`
options.says: every component, var ones included, is read through its accessor

origin.section: Matching Calls the Accessors, and an Exception From One Arrives as MatchException

questions.stem: A teammate writes `for (Pair(var key, var value) : entries) index.put(key, value);`, where `entries` is a `List<Pair>` and `Pair` is a record with two components. What happens when the service is built?

options.text: It compiles, and the loop skips each element that is `null`, since the pattern doesn't match those
options.says: Java 21 has no record patterns in a for header; that was a Java 20 preview that was dropped

options.text: It compiles, and the loop throws on an element that is `null`, since the pattern can't take it apart
options.says: Java 21 has no record patterns in a for header, so there is no run-time behaviour to speak of

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a record pattern may not stand in a loop header in any form, with `var` or without
options.says: the for-header form was a Java 20 preview and was removed in Java 21; javac 21 reports a syntax error

options.text: It doesn't compile, since a record pattern in a loop header needs its component types written out, not `var`
options.says: var is allowed in record patterns; the for header is what Java 21 rejects

origin.section: A Record Pattern Tests the Type, Then Binds Each Component by Position

concepts: A record pattern gets each component by calling its accessor, var components included, so it binds what an overridden accessor returns.
A narrower type on a component is a run-time test, not a cast: a value of another class makes the pattern fail without an exception, and the leftover branch receives it.
In Java 21 a record pattern goes only after instanceof or as a case label; the enhanced-for form was a Java 20 preview that was dropped, and the unnamed pattern _ is a preview until Java 22.
